get.description: The kernel's health, for the load balancer and the smoke checks; no cookie is read.

post.description: A fresh copy of the Rivera seed for whoever holds the passcode, and the owner cookie for it.
A fresh copy for an owner who already has one; the old copy is left as it is, and the cookie moves on.

get.description: The copy the owner cookie names.
The copy's businesses, each with its Desks, in the order the Desks were made: the Desk switcher.

put.description:
The Answering switch, set by the kernel with the owner's credential. Off, visitors can only leave their
details or ask for a callback; the owner's own previews keep every tool.

get.description:
Today on the Desk, computed from the rows on each read (so polling never empties it): how many things need the
owner, the live conversations, the briefing since 18:00 yesterday and the last 7 days, in the business's time
zone.

Every briefing item since 18:00 yesterday in the business's time zone, newest first: the list Today's
briefing links to.
The Desk's conversations, the latest activity first; the owner's own previews included.

A conversation on one of the copy's Desks, as the owner sees it, after the cursor `after` (polled every 2 s).
The cursor never skips a row: a session's rows commit in the order of their `n`.

The attempts the checkpoint stopped on the Desk, newest first: refused requests and replies of Claude's it
blocked (the "stopped" Today counts).

The copy's Demo inbox, read from the kernel with the owner's credential. Its bodies can hold verification
codes, so the answer is never stored, here or in a cache.

The Desk's signed ledger, verified by the kernel on every read (its chain, `first_bad_seq` and key), passed
on unchanged.

parameters.name: verify

schema.description: Always true: the kernel verifies every read
schema.title: Verify

parameters.description: Always true: the kernel verifies every read

get.description:
What waits for the owner on the Desk: each held request as the kernel has it now (read with the owner's
credential, which applies expiry), oldest first, then each open callback request.

post.description:
Mark a callback request done, through the kernel with the owner's credential. A handoff that isn't on one of
the copy's Desks is 404 and never sent; one already done is the kernel's 409 `conflict`.

get.description:
A decision of the copy as the kernel signed it, read with the owner's credential (which applies expiry). One of
another copy is the kernel's 404; a decision the kernel answered for that isn't on one of the copy's Desks is 404
too, so no other copy's record is ever passed on.

post.description:
The owner's answer to a held request. The kernel decides it with the owner's credential, and an allow runs
there and then, as the visitor's session (also during a take-over); the visitor sees the outcome, and Claude
follows up, once the resume job ran and the visitor's own credential is present (the open stream or the next
request). Drafted rule cards come back in `card_diff`; proving them is a rules route's work, so an answer never
waits on a proof.

When the kernel refuses the answer (409: answered before, expired or cancelled) or its response is lost, the
decision is read as it stands: once it left `held`, an outcome the visitor wasn't shown yet gets the (idempotent)
resume job, so a lost response still resumes the chat, and the answer is 409 `already_resolved` with the
decision. A decision still `held` keeps the kernel's own error, its code included ("Errors"): a 409 is
`{error: "kernel", code}`, and an answer that never reached the kernel is 503, `seed_unproved` and `internal`
kept. A decision that can't be read is 503 `kernel_unavailable`. In each case answering again is safe. An answer
the request doesn't offer is the kernel's 422 `invalid`.

get.description:
The Desk's public page: the kernel's `PublicDesk`, unchanged. Never cached: the page's open status refetches
on a delay that assumes a fresh answer (CloudFront doesn't cache `/api/*` either).

Where agents send their requests and how they sign them, built by code from `PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, never from the
request's own host headers. The kernel's public Desk is read only to answer 404 for an unknown slug.

post.description:
The visitor's session on the slug's Desk: the one the cookie holds while the kernel says it is open there (a
returning visitor), else a new one, whose token only the cookie holds. Resuming is never limited, however often a
page reloads (it creates nothing), and is ledgered as a `session` event at most once per session every ten
minutes; a new chat counts toward `new_chat`.

get.description:
The session's state and its transcript as the visitor sees it: their own words and what was delivered to
them, never model, note, owner-only or other sessions' rows. `last_seq` is read in the same snapshot, so the
event stream opened after it neither misses nor repeats an item.

post.description:
Store the visitor's message and start Claude's turn; the answer arrives on the event stream.

A message that starts a model turn (mode `ai`) counts toward the turn limits, per conversation and per address,
and past either is refused before anything is stored. Then what control rows left for this session is done
first, so an outcome that came in meanwhile precedes the message and the same turn answers both. The message
wakes a turn unless the owner has taken the chat over (mode `owner`: the owner answers it). In a paused session
that turn is the kernel's handoff, with no model call: it runs under the session's turn lock and stops the waiting
work from starting more turns, so one handoff answers the message and whatever else was waiting. Neither counts
toward the turn limits.

get.description:
The session's events after the cursor, then live ones (SSE `id` is the event's `seq`). On opening, and as each
control row appears while it is open, the session's runner does what control rows left and runs waiting work,
with the visitor's credential, in a task of its own: a hang-up never cuts it short. Three streams per session
and thirty per address may be open at once: a session's fourth closes its oldest (opening a stream is never
refused for its session's streams, so a reload never is), and past the address's thirty it is 429.

post.description:
Withdraw one of the visitor's own held requests. The kernel cancels it (409 once it is no longer held, 404
for another session's); its signed outcome is then shown as `resolved`, and Claude reads it at the next turn
(an `action_update` that starts none: the visitor already sees what happened).

AgentCardOut.title: AgentCardOut
AgentCardOut.description:
`GET /api/public/desks/{slug}/agent_card`: built by code from `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` and the slug, with no model
text; what agents may do here, and the AI disclosure, are the kernel's `PublicDesk.agent_card`.

AgentCardSigning.title: AgentCardSigning
AgentCardSigning.description: How an agent signs each request: the headers it sends and the payload its Ed25519 signature covers.

AlreadyResolved.title: AlreadyResolved
AlreadyResolved.description:
409: the request was no longer waiting for an answer (answered before, expired or cancelled); `decision` is
how it stands now, as the kernel signed it.

AnsweringIn.title: AnsweringIn
AnsweringIn.description:
`PUT /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/answering`: the Answering switch. Off, visitors can only leave their details
or ask for a callback.

ApiError.title: ApiError
ApiError.description:
Every error answer: `error` names what went wrong; `code` is the kernel's, when `error` is "kernel";
`retry_after` is the seconds to wait, on a 429. Fields that don't apply are left out.

ApprovalAnswerIn.title: ApprovalAnswerIn
ApprovalAnswerIn.description: `POST /api/owner/approvals/{decision_id}/answer`: one of the four answers to a held request.

ApprovalAnswerOut.title: ApprovalAnswerOut
ApprovalAnswerOut.description:
The answered request as the kernel signed it, how its execution went (an allow runs inside the answer; None
for a denial or a request the rules no longer allow), and the rule cards an `allow_person` or `deny_always`
answer drafts, which the owner proves and confirms through the rules routes (Plan 02b).

Attempt.title: Attempt
Attempt.description:
An attempt the checkpoint stopped (`GET /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/safety`): a refused decision (`ref_id` its
`decision_id`) or a reply of Claude's it blocked (`ref_id` the reply entry's `seq`, as text). `reason_plain` is the
kernel's owner text for a decision, or a line the API composes for a reply; `origin` is the ledger entry's;
`ledger_seq` is the entry to show it with. `triage` is AI-written, when there is one.

Briefing.title: Briefing
Briefing.description:
"Since last night": from 18:00 yesterday in the business's time zone (`since`) to now. `total` is the length of
the full list (`BriefingList`).

BriefingItem.title: BriefingItem
BriefingItem.description:
One thing that happened since last night. `ref_id` is what it links to: the attempt's `ref_id` for `blocked`,
the decision for a booking, the `lead_id`, the session for an answer. `line` is the kernel's owner text for a
refusal or a booking, a lead's note (untrusted, as the visitor or Claude wrote it), else None.

BriefingList.title: BriefingList
BriefingList.description: `GET /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/briefing`: every item since last night, newest first.

BriefingNewest.title: BriefingNewest
BriefingNewest.description: The newest blocked attempt, booking, and lead or answer (the lead when both share a time); None when none.

BusinessOut.title: BusinessOut
BusinessOut.description: `GET /api/owner/desks`: one of the copy's businesses, with its Desks (the Desk switcher).

CancelAccepted.title: CancelAccepted
CancelAccepted.description: 202: the held request is withdrawn; its outcome arrives on the event stream as `resolved`.

ConversationSummary.title: ConversationSummary
ConversationSummary.description:
A conversation on the Desk: who it is with (`display_name` as `NeedsYouSession`'s), who has it (`mode`), when
anything last happened in it, how its requests stand (decisions by state), and whether it is the owner's own
preview.

CopyOut.title: CopyOut
CopyOut.description: The owner's copy: what `POST /api/owner/copies`, `start_over` and `me` answer with.

Handoff.title: Handoff
Handoff.description:
An open callback request (`kernel_ro.handoffs`). `reason` is "<name> · <contact> · <reason>" as the visitor
typed them (untrusted text); `callback_window` is "<start>/<end>" in ISO 8601, or None without one.

HealthOut.title: HealthOut
HealthOut.description: `GET /api/health`: 200 with the kernel's health, or 503 with `ok` false and no kernel field.

MessageAccepted.title: MessageAccepted
MessageAccepted.description: 202: the visitor's message is stored; Claude's answer arrives on the event stream.

NeedsYouItem.title: NeedsYouItem
NeedsYouItem.description:
`GET /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/needs_you`: a held request (`decision`, as the kernel signed it when read, which
applies expiry, with `held_by`, the reason of the rule card that held it, and `held_at`, when it was decided) or
an open callback request (`handoff`), never both; who it came from, and the last thing they wrote (untrusted).

NeedsYouSession.title: NeedsYouSession
NeedsYouSession.description:
Who a held request or a callback request came from. `display_name` is the verified person's, else the name
the session's lead gave (untrusted text), else None.

OwnerTranscript.title: OwnerTranscript
OwnerTranscript.description:
`GET /api/owner/conversations/{session_id}?after=n`: the session's state and its transcript after the cursor, as
the owner sees it (agent text, whispers, translations and triage included; model, note and context rows never).

OwnerTranscriptItem.title: OwnerTranscriptItem
OwnerTranscriptItem.description: The owner's view adds the AI-written translation and triage, which never reach a visitor.

ThisWeek.title: ThisWeek
ThisWeek.description:
"Last 7 days": the seven local dates ending today, in `timezone`. Totals run from 00:00 on `start` to now;
`handled + stepped_in == conversations`; `days` holds all seven, oldest first, the last one `end`.

Today.title: Today
Today.description:
`GET /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/today`, computed from the rows on each read. `live` holds the conversations with
activity in the last 5 minutes.

TranscriptItem.title: TranscriptItem
TranscriptItem.description: One transcript entry as the visitor sees it: their own words, or an event the API delivered.

VisitorSession.title: VisitorSession
VisitorSession.description:
`POST /api/public/desks/{slug}/sessions`: the session the visitor cookie now holds, and whether it is the one
the cookie already held (a returning visitor) or a new one.

VisitorTranscript.title: VisitorTranscript
VisitorTranscript.description:
`GET /api/public/desks/{slug}/session`: the session's state, its transcript as the visitor sees it, and the
highest event `seq` read in the same snapshot, which the event stream continues after.
